name: Zerah
overview: Zerah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, specifically identified as a Gershonite, descending from Gershon, son of Levi. He is uniquely noted as the son of Adaiah, situating him within the Levitical lineage responsible for specific priestly duties. His heritage places him among the Levites who served in religious functions according to the Old Testament.
namesAndTitles: The name Zerah means 'dawning, shining or flashing [red or scarlet] light,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This meaning emphasizes brightness or radiance, though the name was not given directly by God but appears in Scripture as a personal name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Zerah was the son of Adaiah. It is also inferred that Ethni was his father, indicating a generational lineage within the Levites. Beyond this, no further family relationships are detailed in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Zerah's significance lies in his place within the Levitical genealogies, particularly among the Gershonites, who were entrusted with important religious responsibilities. His identification as the son of Adaiah connects him to the priestly families serving in the tabernacle or temple. This genealogical record helps preserve the continuity and order of Levitical service as ordained by God.
